summary: The paper extends the Markov-ICL framework to Mamba/selective SSMs, showing empirically that a single-layer Mamba matches the optimal Laplacian (add-β) smoothing estimator on random Markov chains, and providing a constructive proof that a simplified MambaZero can exactly represent the Laplacian estimator for first-order finite-state chains, along with a hidden-dimension lower bound of Ω(2^k) for any recurrent architecture. The convolution-centric ablation and the switching-Markov and WikiText-103 experiments give useful additional evidence. Contributions are novel and mostly well-executed, though the main representation theorem is limited to first-order chains and several empirical claims (e.g., convolution's role in NLP) rest on modest deltas.
strengths: First application of the random Markov / Bayes-optimal predictor framework to Mamba/SSMs, yielding a clean, testable claim (matches add-β Laplacian estimator).

The theoretical package is unusually balanced: a constructive upper bound (Theorem 1) that mirrors the empirically observed parameter structure (a_t≈1, b(ij)c_t≈0 for i≠x_t), plus a matching Ω(2^k) recurrent lower bound (Theorem 2) that gives real architectural insight.
Ablations cleanly isolate convolution as the load-bearing component (MambaZero vs. Mamba-without-conv), and the w ≥ k+1 window-size prediction is empirically confirmed against Markov order.
The switching-Markov experiment is a nice, targeted probe of the selectivity mechanism (a_t) that the pure-Markov setting cannot exercise.
Claims about scope are honestly stated — the paper repeatedly notes that Mamba-vs-Transformers is not the main goal and that higher-order theory is empirical.

key_concerns.issue: Theorem 1 covers only first-order Markov chains; the strong empirical claim in Fig. 1b/10a that Mamba learns the optimal estimator 'for all Markov orders' is not backed by any theorem, and the Ω(2^k) lower bound implies exponential-in-k dimension is required — yet the experiments do not report how the hidden dimension was scaled with k, nor whether performance degrades once d is held fixed while k grows.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Add an experiment sweeping (k, d) to trace the phase boundary predicted by Theorem 2, and either sketch a k-th-order extension of Theorem 1 or scope the abstract/intro claim to first-order + empirical evidence at small k.

key_concerns.issue: Statistical support is thin in places: main figures use only 5 seeds (Fig. 1), and Table 1's WikiText-103 headline (11% for Mamba, 2% for Transformer) is reported for a single 14.5M-parameter run without seeds, confidence intervals, or a matched compute/parameter budget analysis — 'convolution is fundamental' is an appreciably stronger claim than these numbers, especially the transformer 2% delta, can carry.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Report multi-seed means ± std for Table 1 (and Tables 4/5), and either soften language around Table 1 to 'suggestive' or run a larger sweep varying depth/width to establish the effect is not a hyperparameter artifact.

key_concerns.issue: Reliance on empirical parameter regularities (a_t ≈ 1, b(ij)c_t ≈ 0 for i≠x_t, β-summing vectors) is central to Sec. 4.2.1, but the paper treats these as observed conveniences rather than as things to prove or falsify; without a learning-dynamics argument, it is unclear whether the constructive theorem describes what the trained model actually converges to or merely a representable equilibrium.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Either present a parameter-recovery study (compare learned parameters against the theoretical construction quantitatively across seeds), or explicitly frame the theorem as a realizability result and separate it from claims about what training finds.

key_concerns.issue: Related-work positioning against Transformer Markov-ICL work (Edelman et al., Nichani et al., Sanford et al., Rajaraman et al.) is adequate, but the 'first work applying Markov-ICL to Mamba/SSMs' claim would be more convincing with an explicit table contrasting assumptions (depth, order, state size, upper/lower bounds) across these works.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Add a small comparison table in Related Work or Sec. 4 summarizing what is proved for Mamba vs. Transformers in comparable settings.

key_concerns.issue: The extracted equations in Sec. 2.2 are difficult to parse (interleaved column layout, symbols like ex, e_t appearing before definition), and the MambaZero equations in Sec. 4.1 mix (MambaZero) block equations with the outer language-model equations in a way that risks reader confusion.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Rewrite Sec. 2.2 and 4.1 with a single vertical column of numbered equations, define all symbols before use, and add a small diagram/pseudocode of MambaZero.

key_concerns.issue: The dimension-reduction argument for the binary case (d = 2 sufficient, Thm. 4 in appendix) is invoked in the main text but not formally stated; readers cannot evaluate it from the manuscript body.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Include a compact statement of Thm. 4 (assumptions and error bound) in the main text.

questions_for_authors: Theorem 2 gives d·p ≥ 2^k(1−3ε)log(1/ε). What are the actual (d, p) used in the k=1..4 experiments in Fig. 1b, and does performance degrade as predicted when d is held below 2^k?

In the ablation removing convolution (Fig. 3a, Table 1), is the parameter/FLOP budget matched? Table 1's 'w/o conv' has 14.53M vs 14.54M, but width/depth or effective receptive field may not be matched.
The paper states a_t ≈ 1 at convergence for Markov data. Is this stable across seeds, initializations, and Markov orders? A histogram of learned a_t values would help.
How was the WikiText-103 comparison controlled — tokenizer, context length, training tokens, learning rate schedule? The 11% vs. 2% headline is load-bearing for the 'convolution is general' claim.
In the switching-Markov experiment, does Mamba's a_t → 0 behavior at switch tokens emerge for other switch probabilities (e.g., p_switch = 0.1, 0.001), or is it specific to p_switch = 0.01?
Can the L1-normalized prediction layer used in MambaZero be replaced by the standard softmax without breaking the construction, or does the theorem rely on this modification?
calibration_check: Claims are mostly appropriately scoped — the paper acknowledges that the main theorem is first-order and that higher-order results are empirical — but the abstract/intro language of 'learns the optimal in-context estimator for all Markov orders' and 'fundamental role of convolution' outruns the evidence, which is 5-seed empirics up to k=4 and a single-seed 3-point perplexity delta.

significance.justification: Cleanly connects Mamba to a Bayes-optimal statistical estimator and establishes a first Ω(2^k) dimension lower bound for recurrent ICL of Markov chains — likely to be cited by follow-up SSM-theory work.

novelty.justification: First application of the Markov-ICL / random-Dirichlet framework to selective SSMs, and the constructive Laplacian-smoothing representation via convolution + selectivity is not obvious from prior transformer analyses.

rigor.justification: Theorem 1's construction is plausible and its assumptions match observed convergence patterns, and Theorem 2 is a legitimate compression-style lower bound, but several construction steps rely on empirically observed parameter regularities rather than being proved as attractors of training.

statistical_soundness.justification: Main figures use 5 seeds with std bands, which is acceptable, but the load-bearing Table 1 lacks seeds/CIs and no significance testing is reported for ablation deltas.

calibration_honesty.justification: Limitations (first-order theory, learning dynamics out of scope, Mamba-vs-Transformer not the focus) are stated, but 'for all Markov orders' and 'fundamental role' language in the intro/abstract overreaches given the 3-point single-run NLP delta.

clarity.justification: Overall narrative and Sec. 4.2.1 proof sketch are clear, but the extracted equations in Sec. 2.2/4.1 are visually cluttered and use symbols before defining them, which will hinder readers unfamiliar with Mamba-2 internals.

structure_compliance.justification: Standard ICLR structure — Intro/Related/Setup/Empirics/Theory/Extensions/Conclusion — with clear signposting of what is proved vs. observed; length appears well within ICLR norms.

reproducibility.justification: The data-generation process, model equations, training loss, and optimizer are given, and appendices are referenced for hyperparameters; enough to plausibly reproduce given the described methodology, though some specifics (e.g., exact d,N per experiment, WikiText training details) live in appendices not in the body.

related_work.justification: Positioning against Transformer Markov-ICL literature and Mamba expressivity papers is appropriate and mostly complete; would benefit from an explicit comparison table but omission is not fatal.

figure_quality.justification: Figures 1, 3, 5, 13 are directly evidentiary: they show model-vs-optimal-estimator gaps, window/order dependence, learned-parameter regularities used in the proof, and switching a_t behavior — captions convey the claim each figure supports.

breadth_generality.justification: Theory covers first-order finite-state chains only; empirics extend to k up to 4, a switching process, and one WikiText run — sufficient to be interesting but under-supports the intro's 'all orders' and 'general' framing.

overall_recommendation.justification: A well-motivated, technically respectable ICL analysis of Mamba that lands at borderline accept: novel and clean where it is careful, but the k>1 story is empirical-only and NLP evidence is thin.
